_note: Video content for /artist/live-video and the EPK. `uploadDate` is ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) and `durationSeconds` is an integer; both are converted at render time (to a human label, and to an ISO 8601 duration like PT3M58S for VideoObject JSON-LD) so the data stays machine-readable. Every field here was read off the live YouTube watch pages on 2026-07-26 — do not hand-edit durations or IDs without re-checking, because a wrong `duration` in VideoObject is a structured-data error Google will flag.
_thumbnails: YouTube only generates maxresdefault.jpg (1280x720) for some uploads; the 2018 live sessions for `mapa-ni-reloj` and `lejos` only have sddefault.jpg (640x480, 4:3 with letterbox bars). Both are rendered into a 16/9 frame with object-fit:cover, which crops the bars. Verified availability per-ID before choosing the URL — a 404 poster would break the click-to-load facade.

videos.title: Quédate a Mi Lado
videos.subtitle: Live Session
videos.description: Juliana Beltran performs her original song "Quédate a Mi Lado" live with a full band — drums, guitar, keys and bass — in a single-take live session produced by Juan Galeano Toro. Full song, live vocal, no overdubs.
videos.credits: Written by Juliana Beltran. Produced by Juan Galeano Toro. Ale Giuliani (drums), Jose Castillo (guitar), Miguel Rico (keys), Jaime Rubio (bass).
videos._comment: PRIMARY. This is the one a talent buyer should watch: it is the longest of the four live sessions (3:58), a complete song rather than a clip, a live vocal over a live four-piece band, and it has the strongest audio of the set. It is also the only live session with a 1280x720 thumbnail, which matters both for the facade poster and for VideoObject rich-result eligibility. Caveat for whoever maintains this: it was filmed in 2018 and is Spanish-language. If a newer full-song live capture ever exists, promote it — recency is the one axis on which this loses.
